summary: Verified the follow-up fix to the CRITICAL stop-loss retry-loop bug from iteration_30 (ATPC 'insufficient qty available' spam). Code review of position_monitor_service.py confirms `_sell_with_dedup()` is correctly wired into all 3 exit paths (_execute_stop_loss, _handle_partial_take_profit, _check_bearish_crossover_exit) - each now checks alpaca_service.get_open_orders(symbol) before selling, skips the cycle if a sell order <10s old is pending, and cancels+replaces if >=10s stale. alpaca_service.get_orders() fix confirmed: now uses QueryOrderStatus with a safe fallback to ALL for invalid strings (was the wrong OrderStatus enum before, causing ValueError->500). Wrote a deterministic pytest suite (backend/tests/test_stop_loss_dedup_fix.py, 11 tests, all passing) covering: (1) live regression - GET /api/orders?status=open/new/closed/all/bogus_status all return HTTP 200 w/ valid array (previously would 422/500 for non-'all'), (2) unit tests mocking alpaca_service for _sell_with_dedup: fresh pending sell (<10s) -> returns None, no resubmit; stale pending sell (>=10s) -> cancels then places fresh sell; no open orders -> places sell directly; open BUY order on same symbol correctly ignored (dedup is sell-side only); get_open_orders() exception degrades gracefully and still attempts the sell. Live account (PA36RNHPHRUZ) confirmed flat - GET /api/positions and GET /api/orders?status=open both return [] with HTTP 200, matching the problem statement's claim of a clean starting state, so the original ATPC race condition could not be reproduced live (nothing stuck to reproduce against) - the unit-test approach (explicitly pre-approved as acceptable in the review request) was used instead to deterministically verify the fix logic. Ran the FULL backend regression suite (152 tests): 147 passed, 5 pre-existing failures all unrelated to this fix (stale hardcoded paper account number PA30RVV1A2DM in test_auth_and_account_safety.py vs the now-current PA36RNHPHRUZ per test_credentials.md, a renamed scanner_service.news_client attribute, and 2 old asyncio.get_event_loop() WebSocket tests incompatible with current asyncio - none touch position_monitor_service.py or alpaca_service.get_orders()/get_open_orders()).

action_items: No action required for this fix - _sell_with_dedup() and the get_orders()/get_open_orders() QueryOrderStatus fix are correctly implemented and verified deterministically.

Optional/low-priority cleanup (not from this task): update test_auth_and_account_safety.py's hardcoded PA30RVV1A2DM expectation to match the current paper account PA36RNHPHRUZ so that pre-existing test doesn't show as a false failure in future regression runs.
critical_code_review_comments: _sell_with_dedup() correctly distinguishes order side (only treats an existing 'sell' order as blocking - an open buy order on the same symbol is correctly ignored), and degrades gracefully (falls through to placing the sell anyway) if get_open_orders() itself throws, so a data-fetch blip can't permanently block a real exit - good defensive design.

Minor edge case (not a bug, just worth noting): if get_open_orders() throws, the code sets open_orders=[] and proceeds straight to place_market_order without ever checking for an existing order - this means a transient API error during the open-orders check could theoretically still race with a real pending order and hit the original 'insufficient qty' error once, but it will NOT loop indefinitely since the underlying dedup logic still applies correctly on the next 2s cycle. Acceptable tradeoff between availability and strict dedup.

stale_after_seconds=10 default is reasonable given the 2s poll loop (allows ~5 poll cycles for a normal market order to fill before considering it stuck) and matches the review request's expected value exactly.

rca_of_the_issue: N/A - this iteration verifies a fix, not a new bug. Original RCA (iteration_30): position_monitor_service had no de-dup check before submitting exit orders, causing a blind retry every ~2s against an already-pending unfilled sell order and an indefinite 'insufficient qty available' rejection loop. Fix verified: _sell_with_dedup() now checks get_open_orders(symbol) first and either skips (order <10s old), cancels+replaces (order >=10s old, stale), or places directly (no existing order).
